Verification performed at vendoring (2026-09-24):
- asset-sha256 recomputed locally (`shasum -a 256`) equals the asset's line in the
  release's `sqlite3mc-2.5.1-SHA256SUMS`.
- The SHA256SUMS signature (`sqlite3mc-2.5.1-SHA256SUMS.sig`, Sigstore keyless:
  base64-encoded DER ECDSA) verifies with `openssl dgst -sha256 -verify` against the
  public key of the accompanying certificate (`sqlite3mc-2.5.1-SHA256SUMS.pem`,
  base64-encoded PEM): "Verified OK". Certificate: issuer O=sigstore.dev,
  CN=sigstore-intermediate; serial 44DFC0C5A4707D0335EF13E047598F1C1D72F851;
  validity 2026-08-27T16:50:03Z – 17:00:03Z; SAN URI
  https://github.com/utelle/SQLite3MultipleCiphers/.github/workflows/build-reusable.yml@refs/heads/main;
  SHA-256 fingerprint 4A:21:6C:D3:55:F9:6B:3E:92:C3:2A:81:15:EE:2B:39:28:4C:03:8F:16:7E:9B:BD:25:6E:B0:7A:33:7F:E2:2E.
- NOT verified locally (no cosign on the vendoring machine): the certificate chain to
  the Fulcio root and the Rekor transparency-log inclusion. `cosign verify-blob` on a
  machine that has it closes that gap.
- Both files are vendored byte-for-byte from the zip. Not vendored (not build inputs):
  shell3mc_amalgamation.c, sqlite3.h, sqlite3ext.h, README.md.

Re-vendoring (an SQLite3MC release bump): download the new amalgamation zip plus
SHA256SUMS / .sig / .pem, verify as above, replace the two files, update every line of
this record, then run `cargo test -p kupferdraht-core --test step_90_sqlite3mc_engine` — it
pins the header's version defines and the SHA-256 of both files against this record.
